history.summary: The ISKCON Surat temple, the abode of Sri Sri Radha Damodar, was founded in 1978. Founder-acharya Shrila Prabhupada had visited Surat in 1970, and in 1978 the premises with a small Krishna temple were received from the Kanahiyalal Trust, Jahangirpura, initially covering about 900 sq ft. The complex has since grown to about 13,600 sq ft, making it one of the largest temples in Surat. It stands on the banks of the Tapi River on Ashram Road, Jahangirpura, and the temple complex also houses a guest house and shops selling books and souvenirs. Sundays and festivals draw the largest crowds.

name: Sri Sri Radha Damodar Temple (ISKCON Surat)
town_description: Surat is a major city in Gujarat on the banks of the Tapi River, historically one of India's most important ports under Mughal and then British rule. Today it is a thriving metropolis known worldwide as a diamond-processing and textile-manufacturing hub. The city grew from a 12th-century settlement into a Mughal port and later a British stronghold, retaining colonial-era landmarks, old-city bazaars, and a fast-developing riverfront. It is well connected by air, rail, and road to Mumbai, Vadodara, and the rest of Gujarat.

travel.railway: Surat railway station and central bus station, ~15 km
travel.road: Ashram Road, Jahangirpura; Jahangir Pura Teen Rasta and Bhagvati Nagar bus stops nearby; reachable by city bus and auto-rickshaw
